cinematic.body: Begin close on the Caller's leaf pointing to the forbidden previous perch. Move behind the upright screen as the Caller commits, then hold on the public pulse claim while the Watcher chooses Echo or Mimic. End on a clean vertical reveal and the ordered score-then-route update.
cinematic.headline: One flash. Two possible flights.
cinematic.visual_direction: Storyboard a restrained night-garden sequence from the exact digital assembly: inward leaf tip, hidden Flight, 1/2/3 pulse relief, hidden Reply, vertical screen lift, then one leaf advancing while the Caller's leaf rotates. Use no hands, faces, printed texture, or motion claim that would resemble observed human play.

hero.body: False Lantern compresses a complete two-player bluffing duel into six printable parts: a night-garden tray, a sliding lid designed as the intended privacy screen, two reversible selectors, and two score-and-route leaves. Every rule-bearing mark is geometric, so color is optional.
hero.headline: A signal can betray the flight
hero.visual_direction: Use an exact CAD-derived three-quarter play pose. Center the moon-screen vertically between mirrored route docks, with one Flight selector and one Reply selector committed on opposite sides. Keep the surface monochrome and directional, emphasizing relief, pips, leaf tips, and the compact tray rather than implying a physical photograph.

limitations: Exactly two competitive players; no solo, team, or higher-player mode is evidenced.
Age 14+ is a design target, not an age-suitability or toy-safety certification; the design contains small parts and carries a choking-hazard warning.
The proven rules bound is at most nine scoring exchanges. The 5-12 minute target, uncoached teachability, enjoyment, and human-perceived balance have not been verified by human play.

Geometry, fit, motion, sight-ray privacy, mark readability, and anti-roll intent are digital assessments. Physical fit, friction, retention, screen opacity, stability, tactile comfort, wear, drop survival, and durability are unverified.

OrcaSlicer evidence uses a generic Creality Ender-3 PLA profile, not a Bambu-specific profile. It is digital slice evidence, not proof of adhesion, warping behavior, dimensional accuracy, successful printing, or calibrated assembly.
The clearance coupon has not been physically printed or measured. Tune clearances only through a new regenerated and revalidated design revision.
This page-ready package is a private local proposal. It is not evidence of publication, customer availability, manufacture, purchase, shipment, delivery, or customer reviews.
No physical parts, printer, filament, tools, glue, magnets, electronics, batteries, paint, packaging, or loose decoration are represented as supplied.

story_blocks.body: Each Caller's previous route becomes forbidden for both the actual flight and public claim, leaving exactly two legal routes. That constraint follows the role as it swaps, so the public state changes every exchange. Exact strategy analysis gives the opening Caller a 0.5 value, zero maximum duality gap, positive mixing gain in all 25 score states, and no single pure Caller action.
story_blocks.headline: The last perch changes the bluff
story_blocks.visual_direction: Frame the score-and-route leaf as the strategic memory device: one position records 0-5 sparks while one of three tips points inward to record the owner's last route. Pair it with a small two-branch decision diagram, using the same one/two/three-pip grammar as the exact part.

story_blocks.body: If the Watcher's prediction matches the public claim, the reply is an Echo worth one spark. If prediction differs from claim, it is a Mimic worth two. Prediction matching the hidden actual route decides who scores. This separates confidence from correctness: a bolder reply changes the stake without changing the two legal destinations.
story_blocks.headline: Echo one. Mimic two.
story_blocks.visual_direction: Use an exact-selector close view with Flight's two raised wing strokes and Reply's single recessed eye, then a simple split panel labeled Echo 1 and Mimic 2. Preserve crescent and notch ownership marks, broad non-round silhouettes, and geometric rather than color-coded information.

story_blocks.body: The tray carries mirrored docks and score vines; the lid closes the case and stands as the intended keyed privacy screen; two selectors record hidden Flight and Reply choices; two leaves record both score and last route. The closed digital envelope measures 98 x 64 x 12.1 mm, and the modeled storage assembly contains six valid occurrences with no clash above the stated digital tolerance.
story_blocks.headline: Six parts carry the whole state
story_blocks.visual_direction: Use an exploded exact-CAD arrangement above the tray: one tray, one lid, crescent and notch selectors, and the matching one-stud and two-stud leaves. Connect each object to its storage and play pose with thin diagram lines. Do not add accessories, decoration, or fabricated packaging.

story_blocks.body: Digital Playtest retained and replayed 1,600 seeded games across all 16 ordered optimizing, social, exploratory, and adversarial policy pairs. Every trace was legal and terminal within nine scoring exchanges. Exhaustive traversal covered 1,580 reachable states and 7,264 transitions. These are executable digital results, not customer play or enjoyment evidence.
story_blocks.headline: Replayed before release
story_blocks.visual_direction: Treat the evidence as a quiet technical layer: a compact matrix of the four policy families, a 3-9 exchange range, and a thin state graph behind an exact play-pose silhouette. Avoid ratings, testimonials, player portraits, review stars, or emotional-response language.

story_blocks.body: OrcaSlicer 2.3.2 processed all six exact STLs in six separate generic Ender-3 PLA jobs using a 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.20 mm layers, three walls, 15 percent infill, and supports disabled. Hash-bound G-code and native projects report zero errors, zero out-of-bounds parts, and 0.0 g support material. No physical print or calibrated fit is proved.
story_blocks.headline: Real slices, physical claims held
story_blocks.visual_direction: Show a clean six-tile orientation diagram based on the exact meshes, plus restrained process labels and a small generic-profile badge. Do not depict a printer running, finished plastic, hands testing fit, Bambu-specific hardware, filament texture, or a manufacturing receipt.

summary: A six-part, exactly-two-player firefly signaling duel in a 98 x 64 x 12.1 mm digital closed envelope. Secret Flight and Reply selectors turn each legal claim into a one-spark Echo or two-spark Mimic, while the Caller's last route changes the next decision. The package is ready as evidence-bound page copy and printable design data; physical production and human play claims remain unverified.
title: False Lantern

use_case.body: Place the six-part tray between exactly two players, stand the lid in its keyed moon slot, and read the Caller's inward leaf tip as the forbidden route. The Caller commits one legal Flight and announces a legal route; the Watcher predicts with Reply. Reveal, score one-point Echo or two-point Mimic, rotate the Caller's leaf, and swap roles.
use_case.headline: Read, bluff, reveal
use_case.visual_direction: Show a top-down rules tableau derived from exact geometry: score leaves at different posts, the forbidden inward route highlighted, two legal docks available per side, and the screen separating Flight from Reply. Add only plain labels outside the product geometry; color must not carry state.
